newsitem.title: GERMANY: All Nippon Airways expects more demand for Europe.
newsitem.headline: All Nippon Airways expects more demand for Europe.

text.p: All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA) said it foresees growing passenger demand in Japan for European destinations.
Wataru Kubo, senior vice-president and general manager Europe, told Reuters in an interview the airline was looking into new European destinations but it was too early to name any.
Questioned on a possible link-up with Swissair and subsidiary Sabena to offer new Japan-Europe routes, Kubo said only: "That is a very interesting theme which we can look at later."
But he said Brussels was "very attractive" due to the growing numbers of Japanese business travellers visiting European Union institutions there.
ANA currently flies to London, Paris, Frankfurt, Rome, Milan and Vienna from Tokyo and Osaka.
ANA currently flies five weekly code-share flights with Austrian Airlines, in which it has a nine percent shareholding, from Tokyo and Osaka to Vienna.
Swissair is already a partner in the ANA frequent flyer programme, while the airline also has code-share agreements with Delta Air Lines and Air Canada.
Kubo said: "Demand from Japan to Europe is very strong, especially in the tour operator market."
Demand for Europe had fallen slightly this year due to growth in Olympics-related leisure travel to the USA but this was likely to return next year, he added.
Japanese passenger numbers to Europe rose 11.3 percent to 1.8 million in 1995, while European visitor numbers to Japan rose 3.3 percent to 500,000, he noted.
"Italy and Spain are very good destinations for Japanese tourists, Germany and Britain are more for business travellers," Kubo said.
Japanese visitor numbers to Italy rose 32 percent to 366,645 and to Spain by 30 percent to 100,521 last year.
